title: Stochastic phase separation driven by transport noise
summary: Phase separation phenomena occurring in complex fluids are known to be sensitive to hydrodynamic effects: when a binary fluid mixture undergoes spinodal decomposition, the emerging pattern of domains is no longer dictated by interfacial dynamics alone, but is reshaped by advection. In several applications of interest, advection effects may even cause the onset of turbulence, further affecting the segregation process on a wide range of spatial scales.
